sections.presenting_complaint: Cough and coryza for 4 days, increased work of breathing since yesterday.
sections.history: Coryza and cough for 4 days; fast breathing since yesterday. Temperature up to 37.9 °C. Feeding most of his usual amount. Four wet nappies in 24 hours (usually 6–7). Has had an apnoea. No cyanosis. Small posset after coughing. Born at 39 weeks, no neonatal problems. No cardiac or respiratory history. Immunisations up to date.
sections.medications_allergies: Paracetamol once yesterday. No known drug allergies.
sections.examination: Temperature 37.8 °C. RR 54, HR 150, SpO2 95% in air. Intercostal and subcostal recession. CRT under 2 seconds. Alert. Bilateral fine crackles and wheeze.
sections.impression: Bronchiolitis with increased work of breathing (intercostal recession) and feeds about 50% of usual; needs same-day hospital assessment.
sections.plan: Same-day referral to the paediatric assessment unit; paediatric team contacted and expecting him. Small, frequent feeds and saline nose drops before feeds in the meantime. Advised illness may worsen over days 3–5.
sections.safety_netting: Call 999 if pauses in breathing, blue colour, or severe difficulty breathing on the way. Call the practice back if unable to attend within the hour, so an ambulance can be arranged.
